channel.title: Comments for page "Incident Report AMN-C227-939"
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Incident Report AMN-C227-939"

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Replying to a comment 666 days old to ask what you think to be a less "pointlessly grimdark" alternative.

I assume we're talking about setting up and subsequently recruiting J.S. Doing nothing and allowing J.S. to go about his life as if nothing happened for all intents and purposes condemns him to death by inaction; the Foundation has no reason to believe that the long-term effects of AMN-C227 exposure will ever abate. Even with the Foundation's best efforts to search out and destroy 939's dens, there can be no guarantees of his safety if he's allowed to live in ignorance of what he's been exposed to and what it's done to him.

I would further note that there is no actual confirmation that this was even done. This was the recommendation of a Field Agent to their superiors. It's entirely possible that an alternative cover story was concocted and J.S. was never brought in; that, some years later, he had the strangest sense of deja vu in a place he'd never been before and was never heard from again.

item.content:encoded: I'm going to differ from the post above me, and say that I hate how the Foundation acts in this. The Foundation's actions are cold, and feel pointlessly grimdark.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: And I hope this isn't, either, but I'm glad you liked that. That's exactly what that bit was intended to convey. In-universe, they remember why they're doing what they do, and out-of-universe, they're not painted as the lesser of two cartoonish evils.

(Hoping this isn't a necropost)

Personally, I like how the the doctor suggests implicating the guy for murder, but for the purposes of recruiting him as a Level 0 Janitor as opposed to a D-Class. It helps with the image of the Foundation securing, containing, and protecting through any means necessary, but also with the idea that the Foundation is cold, not cruel.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: The "superfluous" added onto "data redacted" feels really unnecessary. The Foundation doesn't redact "superfluous" things, it redacts things that not everyone reading the report need to know, for whatever reason.

item.title: Re: Addendum 03-01-1992: AMN-C227-aided Tracking of SCP-939:
item.content:encoded: Thanks. In my mind, the doctor that wrote it was the same one who authorized AMN-C227 use on civilian populations in the first place, desperately looking for a silver lining and a way to mitigate the consequences of his own oversight.

item.title: Addendum 03-01-1992: AMN-C227-aided Tracking of SCP-939:
item.content:encoded: I am loving the addendum towards the end of this particular article. It describes in vivid detail a situation where an SCP effect can be used to help contain the spread of this particular SCP. More of these ideas throughout the site would greatly improve the scope of the articles.
